question: In the thermogravimetric tests, what sample mass, heating rates, final temperature and purge-gas flow rate were used?
expect: about 5 mg; 5, 10 and 15 C/min; room temperature to 800 C; purge gas 50 mL/min (protective N2 20 mL/min) (sec. 2.3.2)
trap: the STA test's 10 mg and 10 C/min
rendered:
Table 2 from page 2 of the document:

|  | Rock Sample | Specification Test Items | Sample Preparation Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | Test 150−200 mesh | Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) |
|  |  | Simultaneous Thermal Analysis (STA) | Mass Spectrometry Analysis (MS) |
| 2.3.2. Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA). | Thermogravimetric tests were performed using a TGA203F3 thermogravimetric analyzer |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |

And from page 2, section 2.3.1 Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA).

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2.3.2. Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA). | Thermogravimetric tests were performed using a TGA203F3 thermogravimetric analyzer |  |  |
|  |  | For each test, approximately 5 mg of rock sample was weighed into a crucible. |  |
|  |  | Samples were heated from room temperature to 800 °C at 5, 10, and 15 °C min^−1 under air or nitrogen. |  |
|  |  | The reaction purge-gas flow rate was 50 mL min^−1, and the nitrogen protective-gas flow rate was 20 mL min^−1. |  |

So the sample mass used was approximately 5 mg, the heating rates were 5, 10, and 15 °C min^−1, the final temperature was 800 °C, and the purge-gas flow rate was 50 mL min^−1.
